tldr: Canada's Real-Time Rail went live, with Wealthsimple and KOHO already on board, so instant payments are now table stakes for Canadian digital banking. Elsewhere, Venmo's receipt-based bill splitting, Wise's new US savings and stocks products, and stablecoin payments pilots (PNC/Coinbase, Stripe) are shaping new customer expectations.

highlights.headline: Canada's Real-Time Rail launched after years of delay. Wealthsimple joined as instant payments went live, and KOHO announced real-time rail adoption. Interac issued a statement on the launch.
highlights.why: Direct fintech competitors are already positioning on instant payments, so Simplii needs a clear RTR timeline and customer messaging on speed, limits and fees.

highlights.headline: Venmo launched in-app receipt scanning to split bills by item, drawing wide coverage.
highlights.why: It raises the bar for everyday P2P experience; Simplii should check whether Interac e-Transfer flows offer anything comparable for group payments.

highlights.headline: Wise expanded its US offering with Wise Interest and Wise Stocks.
highlights.why: A transfer-first fintech is adding savings and investing to keep deposits on platform, which is the same bundled-money approach that Wealthsimple and EQ Bank use against Simplii's account base.

highlights.headline: PNC is rolling out incoming stablecoin payments for corporate clients with Coinbase. Coinbase also won a full US national trust bank charter, and NYSE plans to settle tokenized stocks on Avalanche.
highlights.why: Crypto and tokenization are moving into mainstream bank and exchange infrastructure. This is not an immediate retail issue, but it is a category shift to watch for payments and trading roadmaps.
